title: Stop Living Paycheck to Paycheck: 5 Phrases for Financial Freedom

subtitles.en:
Hello, everyone! Welcome back to AB Slow
English.
subtitles.zh: 大家好，歡迎再次回到 AB Slow English 的節目。

subtitles.en:
I am Alex, and this is Mia. It is wonderful
to practice English with you today.
subtitles.zh: 我是 Alex，而她是 Mia。今天非常高興能與各位一同練習英文。

subtitles.en:
How are you doing today, Alex? You look very
thoughtful.
subtitles.zh: Alex，你今天好嗎？你看起來若有所思。

subtitles.en:
I was just thinking about a text message,
that I received from a friend, this morning.
subtitles.zh: 我剛才在想，今天早上收到的一位朋友傳來的訊息。

subtitles.en: Oh? What did your friend say?
subtitles.zh: 噢？你的朋友說了什麼呢？

subtitles.en:
He asked: Where did all my money go, this
month? I worked thirty days, but my wallet is
completely empty.
subtitles.zh: 他問我：我這個月的錢都跑去哪裡了？我工作了三十天，但錢包卻空空如也。

subtitles.en:
Oh wow, that sounds painfully familiar, to so
many of us.
subtitles.zh: 天哪，這聽起來對我們許多人來說，真是太過熟悉且令人心痛了。

subtitles.en:
Exactly. In English, we call that living
paycheck to paycheck.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。在英文裡，我們把這種狀態稱為「月光族生活」。

subtitles.en:
Living paycheck to paycheck. It causes so
much daily stress and anxiety.
subtitles.zh: 每個月薪水花得精光，這真的會造成許多的日常壓力與焦慮。

subtitles.en:
But building real wealth, does not require
complicated Wall Street math.
subtitles.zh: 但累積真正的財富，其實並不需要複雜的華爾街數學運算。

subtitles.en:
Really? We do not need complex formulas, or
financial jargon?
subtitles.zh: 真的嗎？我們不需要懂得那些複雜的公式或財經術語嗎？

subtitles.en:
Not at all. True financial freedom begins
with simple daily English phrases, and
mindful habits.
subtitles.zh: 完全不需要。真正的財務自由，始於簡單的日常英文表達與自覺的生活習慣。

subtitles.en:
That is such a relief. Today we will learn
practical phrases, for smart budgeting and
long-term wealth.
subtitles.zh:
那真是太讓人鬆口氣了。今天我們將學習實用的英文表達，
幫助大家聰明規劃預算並累積長期財富。

subtitles.en:
Relax, listen carefully, and let us make our
English always better every day.
subtitles.zh: 請放鬆心情、仔細聆聽，讓我們一起讓英文每天都進步一點點。

subtitles.en:
So Alex, where should we start, on our wealth
building journey?
subtitles.zh: 那麼 Alex，我們的財富累積之旅該從哪裡開始呢？

subtitles.en:
Rule number one is five simple words: Live
below your means.
subtitles.zh: 第一條規則只有五個簡單的字：量入為出。

subtitles.en:
Live below your means. Can you break that
down, for our listeners?
subtitles.zh: 量入為出。你能為我們的聽眾詳細拆解這句話嗎？

subtitles.en:
It means your monthly living costs, must
always be smaller, than your total income.
subtitles.zh: 它的意思是，你每個月的生活開銷，必須始終小於你的總收入。

subtitles.en:
If you earn two thousand dollars, you should
never spend two thousand dollars.
subtitles.zh: 如果你賺了兩千美元，你就絕對不該花掉兩千美元。

subtitles.en:
Right. Even spending nineteen hundred
dollars, gives you a margin of freedom.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。即使只花了一千九百美元，你也能保留一小部分的自由資金。

subtitles.en:
But Alex, social media and ads, make living
below your means so difficult.
subtitles.zh: 但是 Alex，社群媒體和廣告讓量入為出變得好困難。

subtitles.en:
Because modern culture, constantly tempts us,
into impulse buying.
subtitles.zh: 因為現代文化不斷誘惑我們進行衝動購物。

subtitles.en:
Ah, the dreaded impulse buy. Buying something
suddenly, without thinking.
subtitles.zh: 啊，可怕的衝動購物。就是在沒有思考的情況下，突然買了東西。

subtitles.en:
You see a shiny jacket online, your emotions
take over, and you hit checkout, in two
seconds.
subtitles.zh: 你在網路上看到一件好看的外套，情緒一上來，兩秒鐘內就按了結帳。

subtitles.en:
I am so guilty of that. How do we stop those
dangerous impulse buys?
subtitles.zh: 我完全有過這種經驗。我們該如何遏止這種危險的衝動購物呢？

subtitles.en:
Before tapping buy, always ask yourself: Is
this a need, or is this a want?
subtitles.zh: 在按下購買之前，永遠問自己：這究竟是需要，還是想要？

subtitles.en:
A need is essential for survival, like rent,
basic groceries, and medicine.
subtitles.zh: 「需要」是生存所必需的，例如房租、基本食材和藥品。

subtitles.en:
And a want is anything, that just feeds a
temporary emotional desire.
subtitles.zh: 而「想要」則是任何僅能滿足短暫情緒慾望的東西。

subtitles.en:
What should we do, when we desperately want
to buy something non-essential?
subtitles.zh: 當我們非常想買某樣非必要物品時，該怎麼辦呢？

subtitles.en: You must practice, the forty-eight-hour rule.
subtitles.zh: 妳必須練習「四十八小時法則」。

subtitles.en:
The forty-eight-hour rule? What does that
mean?
subtitles.zh: 四十八小時法則？那是什麼意思？

subtitles.en:
It means you tell yourself: I will sleep on
it, for two full days.
subtitles.zh: 意思就是告訴自己：我會冷靜考慮整整兩天。

subtitles.en:
To sleep on it. That means delaying the
purchase, so your head cools down?
subtitles.zh: 冷靜考慮。這意思是延後購買，好讓頭腦冷靜下來嗎？

subtitles.en:
Exactly. Put the item in your cart, walk
away, and go to sleep.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。把物品放入購物車，轉身離開，然後去睡個覺。

subtitles.en:
After forty-eight hours, the shopping fever,
usually disappears completely.
subtitles.zh: 四十八小時之後，那股購物的狂熱通常就會徹底消失。

subtitles.en:
Yes. And you just saved fifty or a hundred
dollars, without any pain.
subtitles.zh: 對。就這樣，你毫不費力地省下了五十或一百美元。

subtitles.en: That is such a powerful mental trick.
subtitles.zh: 這真是一個強大的心理自律技巧。

subtitles.en:
Another smart phrase, to calculate value, is
cost per use.
subtitles.zh: 另一個衡量價值的聰明詞彙是「每次使用成本」。

subtitles.en:
Cost per use? How does that work, in everyday
shopping?
subtitles.zh: 每次使用成本？這在日常購物中該如何運用呢？

subtitles.en:
Divide the price of an item, by the number of
times, you will actually use it.
subtitles.zh: 將物品的價格，除以你實際會使用它的總次數。

subtitles.en:
, , A quality winter coat, worn one hundred
times, has a very low cost per use!
subtitles.zh: 一件穿過一百次的高品質冬裝大衣，分攤下來每次使用的成本其實非常低！

subtitles.en:
, , But a trendy party dress, worn only once,
has an insanely high cost per use.
subtitles.zh: 但如果是一件只穿過一次的流行派對洋裝，那每次使用的成本就貴得嚇人了。

subtitles.en:
, What about peer pressure, Alex?, Social
gatherings can drain a bank account so fast!
subtitles.zh:
Alex，那社交同儕壓力該怎麼辦呢？朋友聚會真的很容易把銀行存款瞬間抽
乾。

subtitles.en:
, Like when coworkers invite you, to an
expensive restaurant for dinner?
subtitles.zh: 比如同事邀請妳去一家人均消費極高的高檔餐廳聚餐嗎？

subtitles.en:
, Yes!, You want to save money,, but you feel
embarrassed saying:, I can't afford it.
subtitles.zh: 對啊！妳想存錢，但又不好意思說出口：「我負擔不起。」

subtitles.en:
, , Never feel ashamed, of protecting your
financial goals, Mia.
subtitles.zh: Mia，為了堅守自己的財務目標而拒絕，永遠都不需要感到羞愧。

subtitles.en:
, What is a polite,, and confident way, to
respond in English?
subtitles.zh: 那有什麼既禮貌又自信的英文說法呢？

subtitles.en:
, You can say:, I'm sticking to a strict
budget this month,, so let's do something
low-key instead.
subtitles.zh: 妳可以說：我這個月正在嚴格執行預算，我們改去個輕鬆平價的地方吧。

subtitles.en:
, I'm sticking to a strict budget!, That
sounds responsible, and mature.
subtitles.zh: 我正在嚴格控制預算！這話聽起來非常有責任感而且很成熟。

subtitles.en:
, And the word, low-key, means casual,
relaxed, and not expensive.
subtitles.zh: 而且 low-key 這個詞的意思是隨性、輕鬆、平價且不鋪張。

subtitles.en:
, Like cooking dinner at home,, walking in
the park,, or grabbing a simple cup of tea!
subtitles.zh: 就像是在家煮頓晚餐、去公園散步，或是喝杯簡單的熱茶！

subtitles.en:
, Exactly., Propose a fun alternative,, and
true friends will gladly join you.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。主動提出一個有趣又無負擔的備案，真正的朋友一定會樂意接受。

subtitles.en:
, In fact,, someone in the group will
probably feel relieved, that you spoke up!
subtitles.zh: 事實上，群組裡肯定會有人因為妳挺身說出這句話而大大鬆了一口氣。

subtitles.en:
, That allows you to cut down on non-
essentials,, while still enjoying your
friendships.
subtitles.zh: 這樣就能讓妳在享受友誼的同時，成功減少非必要的開支。

subtitles.en:
, Cut down on non-essentials!, That means,
reducing unnecessary spending.
subtitles.zh: 減少非必要開銷！意思就是要剔除那些無謂的花費。

subtitles.en:
, Small cuts on non-essentials,, create
massive savings, over time.
subtitles.zh: 長期下來，在非必要開銷上省下的一點一滴，會匯聚成巨大的儲蓄。

subtitles.en:
, Now Alex,, let's talk about the biggest
saving mistake, people make every month.
subtitles.zh: 現在 Alex，讓我們來聊聊大家每個月存錢時最常犯的一個大錯誤。

subtitles.en:
, Most people spend their paycheck first,,
and hope to save, whatever is left over.
subtitles.zh: 多數人領了薪水後會先盡情花費，心想著月底有剩下多少就存多少。

subtitles.en:
, And by day twenty-five,, there is usually
nothing, left to save!
subtitles.zh: 結果通常到了第二十五天，就根本連一毛錢都不剩了。

subtitles.en:
, That is why the wealthy follow this golden
rule:, Pay yourself first.
subtitles.zh: 這就是為什麼有錢人始終遵循這條黃金法則：先把薪水存給自己。

subtitles.en:
, Pay yourself first!, How does that work, on
payday?
subtitles.zh: 先付給自己！在發薪日當天這該怎麼落實呢？

subtitles.en:
, The moment your salary arrives,, transfer
fifteen percent, straight into your savings
account.
subtitles.zh: 薪水進帳的同一時間，就把百分之十五直接轉帳到專屬的儲蓄戶頭。

subtitles.en:
, Before paying the landlord,, and before
buying any takeout food!
subtitles.zh: 在付給房東之前，也在點任何外賣美食之前。

subtitles.en:
, Yes., You treat your future savings,, as
your most important, non-negotiable bill.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。妳必須把未來的儲蓄，當成每個月第一優先、絕不能討價還價的帳單。

subtitles.en:
, And to make it effortless,, you should
automate your savings,, right?
subtitles.zh: 而且為了不考驗人性意志力，應該要設定自動化儲蓄，對吧？

subtitles.en:
, Absolutely., Set up an automatic bank
transfer,, on the day your salary hits.
subtitles.zh: 完全正確。在發薪日當天設定銀行自動定期轉帳。

subtitles.en:
, Out of sight, out of mind!, You can't spend
money, you don't see.
subtitles.zh: 眼不見為淨！只要日常錢包裡看不到這筆錢，妳就根本花不到它。

subtitles.en:
, And your first savings priority,, is
building an emergency fund.
subtitles.zh: 而這筆錢的第一個儲蓄目標，就是建立你的緊急備用金。

subtitles.en:
, An emergency fund!, Also known as,, putting
money away for a rainy day.
subtitles.zh: 緊急備用金！也就是我們常說的「存錢未雨綢繆」。

subtitles.en:
, It gives you a comfortable financial
cushion,, when unexpected life surprises
happen.
subtitles.zh: 當人生突然面臨意外插曲時，它能提供妳一張安心舒適的財務緩衝墊。

subtitles.en:
, Alex,, what happens when someone finally
gets a promotion,, or a pay raise?
subtitles.zh: Alex，那如果有人終於升職或加薪賺比較多錢了，會發生什麼事？

subtitles.en:
, Beware of a sneaky trap,, called lifestyle
creep.
subtitles.zh: 小心一個極度狡猾的隱形陷阱，叫做生活方式膨脹。

subtitles.en:
, Lifestyle creep?, Does that mean your
lifestyle expenses,, creep upward unnoticed?
subtitles.zh: 生活方式膨脹？意思是生活開銷在不知不覺中悄悄往上攀升嗎？

subtitles.en:
, Exactly., As your income rises,, your
expensive habits, quietly expand at the same
speed.
subtitles.zh: 完全正確。隨著收入增加，昂貴的消費習慣也悄悄以同樣的速度膨脹擴張。

subtitles.en:
, You earn more money,, but you buy more
luxury items,, so you save nothing new!
subtitles.zh: 薪水變多了，但買了更多奢侈享受，結果每個月新增的儲蓄依然是零。

subtitles.en:
, And modern subscription services,, make
lifestyle creep, even worse.
subtitles.zh: 而且現代的軟體訂閱制，讓生活方式膨脹的問題變得更嚴重。

subtitles.en:
, Ah, vampire subscriptions!, Ten dollars
here,, twelve dollars there, every month!
subtitles.zh: 啊，吸血鬼訂閱！每個月這裡扣十美元、那裡扣十二美元。

subtitles.en:
, Streaming services, unused gym passes,, and
forgotten mobile apps,, bleed your bank
account.
subtitles.zh:
沒在看的影音平台、沒在去的健身房會籍、忘記刪掉的付費 App，
都在默默放乾帳戶的血。

subtitles.en:
, How often should we audit, our
subscriptions, Alex?
subtitles.zh: 那我們該多常審查一次自己的訂閱扣款呢，Alex？

subtitles.en:
, Once every season,, do a thorough
subscription audit,, and trim the fat.
subtitles.zh: 每隔一季，做一次徹底的訂閱審查，並剔除掉那些浪費的開支。

subtitles.en:
, Trim the fat. That means, cutting out all
the extra waste.
subtitles.zh: 刪減開銷。意思是說，把所有多餘的浪費與開銷通通剪除。

subtitles.en:
, Cancel any subscription, that you haven't
opened, in the past thirty days.
subtitles.zh: 果斷退訂任何在過去三十天內，你根本沒點開過的付費服務。

subtitles.en:
, That simple habit, can easily put, an extra
five hundred dollars, back into your pocket,
every year!
subtitles.zh: 光是這個簡單的習慣，每年就能輕鬆替你省下五百多美元，放回你的口袋裡！

subtitles.en:
, That five hundred dollars, can now go
toward, your long-term wealth building!
subtitles.zh: 而這省下來的五百美元，現在就可以投入到長期的財富累積當中！

subtitles.en:
, Which brings us, to the ultimate secret of
wealth: compound interest!
subtitles.zh: 這就帶我們來到了財富的核心終極秘密，也就是複利效應！

subtitles.en:
, Albert Einstein, reportedly called compound
interest, the eighth wonder of the world.
subtitles.zh: 相傳愛因斯坦曾稱複利，是世界第八大奇蹟。

subtitles.en:
, How does compound interest, actually work,
in simple English?
subtitles.zh: 用最簡單的生活英文來說，複利到底是如何運作的呢？

subtitles.en:
, Think of the snowball effect. A small
snowball, rolling down a snowy hill, gets
bigger and bigger.
subtitles.zh: 想想看滾雪球效應。從小小的雪球從雪山頂滾下，會越滾越大。

subtitles.en:
, Your saved money, earns interest, and then
that interest, earns more interest!
subtitles.zh: 你存下來的錢會產生利息，而這些利息又會繼續滾出更多利息！

subtitles.en:
, Over time, your money starts working, much
harder, than you ever could, with your two
hands.
subtitles.zh: 時間一長，金錢為你工作的辛勤程度，會遠遠超過你自己用雙手勞動的極限。

subtitles.en:
, That is the difference, between working for
money, and having your money, work for you!
subtitles.zh: 這就是為了錢賣命工作，與讓金錢為你工作之間的最大差別！

subtitles.en:
, And you don't need, huge sums to start.
Even ten dollars a day, invested wisely,
grows exponentially.
subtitles.zh:
而且你不需要龐大本金才能開始。哪怕每天只聰明地存下十美元，
日後都會呈指數級成長。

subtitles.en:
, That is why slow wealth, always beats, get-
rich-quick schemes.
subtitles.zh: 這就是為什麼慢富哲學，永遠能擊敗那些一夜暴富的虛妄騙局。

subtitles.en:
, Getting rich slowly, takes discipline, but
it almost never fails.
subtitles.zh: 慢慢變富需要自律，但它幾乎從不失靈。

subtitles.en:
, Budgeting, is not about deprivation, or
feeling poor.
subtitles.zh: 認真做預算，從來不是為了苛待自己，也不是為了體驗貧窮。

subtitles.en:
, Budgeting is about choosing, what truly
matters, so you can purchase, your future
freedom.
subtitles.zh: 做預算是為了選擇真正重要的人事物，好為自己買下未來的自由。

subtitles.en:
, What a beautiful, and empowering, mindset
shift, Alex!
subtitles.zh: 這真是一個美麗而且給予人滿滿力量的思維轉變，Alex！

subtitles.en:
, Now let's practice, these life-changing
phrases, with our slow shadowing session!
subtitles.zh: 現在就讓我們進入慢速跟讀環節，大聲把這些能改變一生的實用句子練熟吧！

subtitles.en:
, Listen closely, to Alex's slow
pronunciation, and repeat after him, out
loud!
subtitles.zh: 請大家仔細聆聽 Alex 的清晰慢速發音，跟著他在後頭大聲唸出來！

subtitles.en: , Number one: Always live, below your means.
subtitles.zh: 第一句：永遠保持量入為出。

subtitles.en:
, Sentence two: When you want to impulse buy,
sleep on it, for forty-eight hours.
subtitles.zh: 第二句：當你想衝動購物時，先放一放，考慮四十八小時。

subtitles.en:
, Number two: Sleep on it, for forty-eight
hours.
subtitles.zh: 第二句：考慮四十八小時。

subtitles.en:
, Sentence three: I'm on a strict budget, so
let's do something, low-key.
subtitles.zh: 第三句：我正在嚴格控制預算，我們改去個輕鬆平價的地方吧。

subtitles.en:
, Number three: Let's do something, low-key
instead.
subtitles.zh: 第三句：改去平價輕鬆的地方聚聚。

subtitles.en:
, Sentence four: On every payday, always pay
yourself first.
subtitles.zh: 第四句：在每個發薪日，永遠第一時間先付錢給自己。

subtitles.en: , Number four: Always pay yourself first.
subtitles.zh: 第四句：永遠先存錢給自己。

subtitles.en:
, Sentence five: An emergency fund, provides
a comfortable, financial cushion.
subtitles.zh: 第五句：緊急備用金能提供一張安心舒適的財務緩衝墊。

subtitles.en:
, Number five: Build a comfortable, financial
cushion.
subtitles.zh: 第五句：建立一張舒適的財務安全墊。

subtitles.en:
, Wonderful job practicing, with us today,
everyone!
subtitles.zh: 大家今天跟著我們一起練習，表現得實在太棒了！

subtitles.en:
, Your spoken English, and your financial
mindset, are growing stronger, every day!
subtitles.zh: 你們的英語口說能力與財富思維，每天都在變得更加強大！

subtitles.en:
, And now, it is time for our favorite part:
The Daily Challenge!
subtitles.zh: 現在，又到了我們最愛的環節，每日互動挑戰！

subtitles.en:
, We want to hear from you, in the comments
section, below!
subtitles.zh: 我們好想在下方的留言區聽到大家的聲音！

subtitles.en:
, What is one non-essential item, or
subscription, that you stopped buying, to
save money?
subtitles.zh: 最近有哪一樣非必要的物品或訂閱服務，是你為了省錢而停買或退訂的呢？

subtitles.en:
, Write your answer, in simple English below.
Mia and I, read every single comment!
subtitles.zh: 請試著在下方用簡單的英文回答。Mia 和我會親自閱讀每一則留言喔！

subtitles.en:
, If you enjoyed this lesson, please like
this video, subscribe to AB Slow English, and
share it, with your friends!
subtitles.zh:
如果你喜歡今天的課程，請幫影片點個讚、訂閱我們的頻道，
並分享給身邊的朋友！

subtitles.en:
, Thank you for spending, this peaceful time
with us. And always remember:
subtitles.zh: 非常感謝大家今天與我們共度這段寧靜充實的時光。請永遠記住——

subtitles.en: , Always Better Everyday.
subtitles.zh: 每天都在變得更好。

subtitles.en:
, We will see you, in the next episode. Stay
safe, and keep learning!
subtitles.zh: 我們下一集再見。祝大家平安順心，持續學習進步！

subtitles.en:
, See you next time, on AB Slow English! Bye-
bye!
subtitles.zh: 我們下次在節目中相見囉！拜拜！
